title: The baby who spoke
hook: Maryam carries her baby home, says nothing to the accusations, and points to the cradle

segments.voice: Yesterday, an-nakhlah, the palm tree: Maryam in labor, a stream beneath her, dates falling. Your line was shake the tree; eat; be glad.

Maryam is walking home: unmarried, carrying a newborn, toward the people who know her family. There's no way to explain this. Any explanation she gives will sound like an excuse. Under the palm tree she was told what to do: if you meet anyone, say, I have vowed a fast to the Most Merciful, and I will not speak to anyone today. A fast of silence. So she walks into town, into the stares, and the voices start. O Maryam, you've done a terrible thing. Your father was a good man. Your mother was a decent woman. Maryam says nothing at all. She just points at the baby.
screen: `CARRYING HIM HOME.` → `A FAST OF SILENCE.` → `SHE POINTS AT THE BABY.`

segments.voice: They're baffled. In Pickthall's words: “How can we talk to one who is in the cradle, a young boy?” And then the baby speaks. “Lo! I am the slave of Allah. He hath given me the Scripture and hath appointed me a Prophet.” His first words aren't about himself as a wonder; they're about who he serves. Allah has made me blessed wherever I am, he goes on, told me to pray and give charity as long as I live, and to be kind to my mother. Not arrogant, not wretched. Then this line: “Peace on me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I shall be raised alive!” If that sounds familiar, it should. A few verses earlier the Qur'an says almost the same words about Yahya, the son of nida'an khafiyya. Two prophets, two impossible births, one blessing. Notice who does the defending. Maryam doesn't argue or prove anything. She keeps her silence, and the truth speaks for her, from the cradle. One detail scholars discuss: the crowd calls her sister of Harun, of Aaron. Muslims understand this as a family or priestly connection, or a brother named Harun, not a claim that she was Musa's sister; a hadith in Sahih Muslim says people used to be named after earlier prophets and good people. Muslims count the cradle among Isa's miracles, and another surah names it too: he spoke to people in the cradle, and his first words cleared his mother's name.
screen: `HOW CAN WE TALK TO A BABY?` · `I AM THE SLAVE OF ALLAH.` · `PEACE ON ME THE DAY I WAS BORN.` · `SHE KEEPS SILENT; THE TRUTH SPEAKS.` · then, large: `LET THE TRUTH SPEAK.`

segments.voice: Keep a small fast of silence, as Maryam vowed to speak to no one that day: say nothing, and try to say nothing inside too. When your mind starts drafting a reply, an explanation, a defense, notice it, leave it unsent, and come back to the quiet. If you pray, you can leave your defense with Allah, as Maryam did.
Al-mahd, the cradle: where the infant Isa spoke his first words, I am a servant of Allah, while Maryam kept her silence.
Your line: let the truth speak. Tomorrow, who Isa is for Muslims. That's day seventy-three.

howItsDone: Muslims read the story of Isa speaking in the cradle in Surah Maryam, and his words, peace on me the day I was born, are recalled as a blessing on birth, death and rising.

what it means: Maryam keeps silent, and the truth defends her; the child's first words say whose servant he is.
what a scholar hears: 'abd Allah, the slave or servant of Allah, is his first self-description; and the blessing in 19:33 mirrors the one on Yahya in 19:15, joining the two prophets.

notes: Pickthall 19:29, 19:30 and 19:33 quoted from memory; confirm exact wording and punctuation.
'Sister of Harun' (19:28): explanations summarized (priestly line of Aaron; a brother named Harun; naming after prophets per Sahih Muslim 2135). Hadith number from memory; confirm.
'Muslims count this as the first miracle of Isa': also listed in 5:110 ('thou spakest unto mankind in the cradle'); confirm the phrasing 'first'.
'Two cousins': Yahya and Isa are described as maternal cousins in hadith (e.g. the Mi'raj narrations 'the two cousins'); confirm.
